findings.explanation: The module declares and validates cache.connect_mode (DIRECT_PEERING|PRIVATE_SERVICE_ACCESS) but the resource sets connect_mode = "PRIVATE_SERVICE_ACCESS" literally, so the input is dead. example/examplea is documented (and holden:ignore'd for HLD_GCP_146) as a DIRECT_PEERING example and passes a CIDR reserved_ip_range (192.168.0.0/28); with PSA forced, reserved_ip_range must be the name of an allocated PSA range, so that example cannot apply as written. HLD_GCP_146/HLD_GCP_254 evaluate the hardcoded literal and so can never see what a caller actually asked for.
findings.remediation: Use the input with PSA as the default: connect_mode = coalesce(var.cache.connect_mode, "PRIVATE_SERVICE_ACCESS"), and set connect_mode = "DIRECT_PEERING" explicitly in example/examplea.
findings.resolution: fixed: connect_mode = coalesce(var.cache.connect_mode, "PRIVATE_SERVICE_ACCESS") keeps PSA as the default for callers that omit it; example/examplea now sets connect_mode = "DIRECT_PEERING" (verified in tofu plan). Callers that already passed DIRECT_PEERING will now get it, which forces replacement of their instance.
findings.title: cache.connect_mode input is ignored: connect_mode is hardcoded to PRIVATE_SERVICE_ACCESS

findings.explanation: Validations check read_replicas_mode values and that replica_count is set when READ_REPLICAS_ENABLED, but not that read replicas need STANDARD_HA. A BASIC instance with READ_REPLICAS_ENABLED (or replica_count > 0) passes validate/plan and is rejected by the Memorystore API at create time. Principle is a best fit: an apply-time correctness gap.
findings.resolution: fixed: added a cache validation in variables.tf requiring tier STANDARD_HA for read replicas.
findings.title: Read replicas can be requested on BASIC tier; the module only fails at apply time

findings.explanation: maintenance_policy is optional and null by default, so the dynamic block renders nothing and Google may apply maintenance (with a failover on STANDARD_HA) at any time, including business hours. Both STANDARD_HA examples omit it, so the module's documented usage ships without a window. No built-in holden policy covers google_redis_instance.maintenance_policy.
findings.remediation: Set cache.maintenance_policy (e.g. { day = "SUNDAY", hours = 3, minutes = 0 }) in the examples; see suggested policy LOCAL_GCP_001.
findings.resolution: fixed: examplea and exampleb set maintenance_policy (SUNDAY 03:00); LOCAL_GCP_001 installed to enforce it. Module input stays optional (non-breaking).
findings.title: No maintenance window: the module defaults maintenance_policy to null and no example sets one

findings.explanation: persistence_config is optional and null, so instances run with persistence disabled: a full-instance failure or a BASIC-tier node loss drops all data with no snapshot to restore from. For a pure cache that is acceptable; for Redis used as a counter/session store (examplea is named "counter") it is data loss. Medium confidence: depends on the workload.
findings.remediation: Enable RDB snapshots where data must survive: persistence_config = { persistence_mode = "RDB", rdb_snapshot_period = "TWELVE_HOURS" }. Validate persistence_mode values in variables.tf.
findings.resolution: fixed: RDB persistence is now the module default. cache.persistence_config is optional with default {} and persistence_mode defaults to "RDB", rdb_snapshot_period to "TWELVE_HOURS"; the persistence_config block is always rendered. Opt out for pure-cache workloads with persistence_config = { persistence_mode = "DISABLED" } (snapshot period is then sent as null). rdb_snapshot_period is validated. Breaking: existing callers that omitted persistence_config get RDB enabled in place on next apply.
findings.title: RDB persistence is off by default and in every example

findings.explanation: A plain `holden scan` only scans example/examplea for Terraform. examplec exists solely to exercise the redis-cluster policies (HLD_GCP_195/196) and exampleb is the only PSA path (google_compute_global_address + google_service_networking_connection), yet neither is ever evaluated by the default scan, so regressions there go unreported.
findings.fix:
- path: example/exampleb
    targets: [terraform]
  - path: example/examplec
    targets: [terraform]
findings.remediation: Add example/exampleb and example/examplec to scan_roots with targets: [terraform].
findings.resolution: fixed: example/exampleb and example/examplec added to .holden.yaml scan_roots; the default scan now evaluates them (surfacing existing deterministic findings on examplec's network fixture).
findings.title: .holden.yaml scan_roots omit example/exampleb and example/examplec

suggested_policies.rationale: Missing maintenance_policy on google_redis_instance is a single-attribute, unambiguous check that applies to any Memorystore Redis instance, and no built-in policy covers it (coverage_by_type lists HLD_GCP_144/145/146/251/254/255/263/329, none on maintenance_policy).
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: LOCAL_GCP_001
name: Memorystore Redis instances should define a maintenance window
principle: reliability
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  Without a maintenance_policy, Google applies Memorystore maintenance at any
  time. On STANDARD_HA this triggers a failover and on BASIC a full restart,
  so unscheduled maintenance can land in business hours.
message: |
  google_redis_instance {{ .ID }} has no maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_window.
remediation: |
  Add a maintenance window:
    maintenance_policy {
      weekly_maintenance_window {
        day = "SUNDAY"
        start_time {
          hours   = 3
          minutes = 0
        }
      }
    }
resources:
  google_redis_instance:
    path: maintenance_policy
    not_null: true
